Natalie: heads-up — dashboard % change for 'quant-v2.1' evals shows -9.2% accuracy but the raw CSV summary shows -3.7%. Noticed this after the night CI run, looks like the chart diff is overstating the regression. Anyone seen this? /cc @Omar

Omar: I skimmed the export earlier, same discrepancy. My hunch: UI is averaging per-shard percent changes instead of computing a weighted percent change from the aggregated counts.

Matt: can you paste the export sample and dashboard link? want to repro locally.

Natalie: dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/quant-v2.1/2026-03-18
Export snippet (s3 path): `s3://eval-exports/quant-v2.1/2026-03-18.csv`
Quick CSV head:
```
metric,base,new,delta,delta_pct,examples
accuracy,0.721,0.655,-0.066,-9.2,1250
accuracy,0.718,0.692,-0.026,-3.7,1250
```
(note: second line is the weighted aggregate we compute in the summary)

Omar: aha — the chart "percent change" series is computed as `mean(delta_pct)` across shards. for very imbalanced shard sizes that blows up the visual. The CSV we export computes the aggregated metric and then the percent change, which is the correct approach.

Laura: confirmed. reporting-service v0.34 introduced a change to the chart aggregator to just average percent deltas to speed up rendering. That was a mistake for metrics that require weighting by example counts.

Sujit: repro details: our runner shards the test set by split sizes [1000, 200, 50]. Example-level weighting matters. average of per-shard pct changes = ( -6.6% + -13.0% + -9.5% )/3 = -9.7% vs weighted = -3.7%. huge difference.

ci-bot: [automated] flaky-runner/quant-v2.1 failed threshold: accuracy dropped beyond allowed delta. Re-run queued.

Matt: suggested fix in words: compute the aggregate numerator and denominator across shards and then compute pct change from the aggregated metrics (i.e., do not average percentages). Proposed code change in reporting-service:
```
# WRONG
pct_change = mean([ (new_i - base_i)/base_i for i in shards ])
# RIGHT
agg_base = sum(base_i * n_i for i in shards)
agg_new  = sum(new_i * n_i for i in shards)
pct_change = (agg_new - agg_base) / agg_base
```
Also add an assertion test in CI that dashboard.percent_change ~= export.percent_change within tiny epsilon.

Natalie: do we need a hotfix? this is visible on the canary front page and will confuse PMs.

Omar: I'll open a PR to reporting-service and dashboard-renderer. It's a small change but affects chart API contract so we should add a migration test. I'll mark it for hotfix if the CI rerun doesn't clear.

Sujit: I'll add a CI job that runs after evals: compare dashboard API response to exported CSV aggregated row for every metric in the run. If mismatch > 0.5% fail the job. Also will emit `shard_counts` in the eval manifest so dashboard has the needed weights.

Matt: I'll add a release note and ping growth/docs about the visualization behavior. We should call out that per-shard averages are NOT reliable for aggregate metrics.

Laura: I'll prepare a patch branch to cherry-pick to prod if needed. Also add a small banner in the UI for now: "Percent-change uses weighted aggregates — if you see large discrepancies check export."

Natalie: action items recap: Omar opens PR for reporting-service + dashboard change; Sujit adds CI test and eval-manifest shard_counts; Laura readies prod patch; Matt updates release notes and docs. ETA: tomorrow 12:00 PT. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Omar: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/reporting/pulls/892 — includes unit tests and a note to frontend to use the new `agg_pct_change` field.

Sujit: CI test PR: https://git.redwood.ai/eval-harness/pulls/457 — runner emits manifest with `shard_counts` and asserts dashboard vs csv aggregated values.

Natalie: perfect. once CI green, coordinate a small rollback window if anything else breaks. keeping this thread updated.

eval-bot: [info] rerun complete: flaky-runner/quant-v2.1 — weighted accuracy delta now matches dashboard after fix (+0.3% diff).

Natalie: closing the loop — regression was overestimated due to averaging bug, fix deployed to prod charts, CI test merged. thanks everyone. :rocket:
